ops.title: cc-pool v0.21-native redesign: ownership fencing, upgrade migration, pool, observation lane
ops.body:
Inputs: verdict note efa8ce2 (daemonkit store; its measurement section stands), mechanical-lane note 0f6686e (branch dk-v021-migration @ bf52839, worktree /private/tmp/w5-cc-pool). Owner decision, verbatim: "change cc-pool to the new design, dont try to port bad old design." All cites below verified against cc-pool origin/main 8df819e, daemonkit v0.21.3 (docs/DESIGN.md, docs/MIGRATING-0.21.md), fusekit b313adf, synckit v0.37.1.

## A. Ownership + fencing successor

### The old fence, as verified

- Fence value: CredentialOperationFence{Token, Owner proc.Record, Epoch uint64} (internal/store/credential_operation.go:282). Every fenced write is a SQL CAS on (token, owner_record, owner_epoch): StageCredentialOperationPublication (:831-835), settleCredentialOperation's DELETE (:1052-1056), advanceCredentialOperation (:1739-1748), AbandonPreparedCredentialOperation (:1199-1202); pending_adds equally in ReleaseAccountIndex/consumeReservation (internal/store/reserve.go:70, :89) and PendingAddReservationsOwnedBy (:328-343); account_mutations mirror it (internal/store/account_mutation.go).
- owner_record bytes = json.Marshal(proc.Record) (encodeCredentialOwner :2707; the 16-field struct at daemonkit@v0.20.9/proc/reaper.go:58); equality is canonical-bytes equality (sameCredentialOwner :2736), in Go and in SQL.
- Owner mint: pool.Manager.credentialOwnerRecord (internal/pool/manager.go:24) = proc.CurrentIdentity() + reaper.TrackIdentity(..., CredentialOwnerRecoveryID) (internal/pool/workers.go:74, :27) — the daemon tracks ITS OWN identity in the worker FileStore so a successor's reaper can mint a durable ReapReceipt for it.
- Takeover: TakeoverCredentialOperation (:1074) requires verifyProcessRetirement (:1139-1160): a valid proc.ReapReceipt whose Record equals the dead owner and whose ReaperGeneration equals the new owner's generation, verified by the reaper — then the epoch CAS: SET owner_record=new, owner_epoch=owner_epoch+1 WHERE token=? AND owner_record=old AND owner_epoch=? (:1113-1119).
- Recovery driver: the receipt feed (internal/pool/credential_recovery.go:26 RecoverRetiredCredentialOwners, called at daemon boot from startProductRuntime, internal/daemon/transport.go:230): page ReapReceipts per CredentialOwnerRecoveryID; per receipt take over / settle every row OwnedBy(receipt.Record); AcknowledgeReap only when zero rows remain (:180-200). The un-acked receipt is the durable cross-crash work list.

### The successor

New owner identity, cc-pool-owned — internal/store/owner.go (new file):

    type OwnerRecord []byte // canonical bytes; the SQL equality key, opaque once stored

    type ownerIdentity struct {
        V       int    `json:"v"`       // 2 — no proc.Record era ever wrote this
        PID     int    `json:"pid"`     // diagnostic
        Started int64  `json:"started"` // unixnano, diagnostic
        Nonce   string `json:"nonce"`   // 16 random bytes hex — the identity
    }

    func MintOwnerRecord(now time.Time) (OwnerRecord, error) // json.Marshal(ownerIdentity{...}); deterministic (fixed struct, declaration order)
    func (o OwnerRecord) Validate() error                    // non-empty, <= 1 KiB

- Minted once per daemon generation inside Start; pool.Manager holds it as a field (Manager.owner OwnerRecord), replacing credentialOwnerRecord()/MutationOwner()'s per-call proc.CurrentIdentity (manager.go:24, :43). No persistence: after a crash nobody needs the old bytes decodable, only comparable.
- Store retypes: CredentialOperationFence.Owner, CredentialOperation.Owner (:289), PendingAccountReservation.Owner, the account-mutation owner, BeginCredentialOperationRequest.Owner (:367), BeginAccountMutationRequest (account_mutation.go:182), ReserveAccountIndex(owner) (reserve.go:30) all become OwnerRecord. sameCredentialOwner becomes bytes.Equal; encodeCredentialOwner/mustEncodeCredentialOwner/decodeCredentialOwner (:2707-2740) delete; scanCredentialOperation (:1816) keeps the raw column bytes without decoding. pool/credential_operation.go:130's `boundary.operation.Owner != owner` becomes !bytes.Equal.
- Every SQL CAS site is unchanged: same columns, same WHERE, same epoch bump.

Retirement proof moves from a verified receipt to Serve's flock:

- Delete: ProcessRetirementVerifier (:20), verifyProcessRetirement (:1139), the receipt+verifier parameters of TakeoverCredentialOperation (:1074) and its account-mutation sibling, CredentialOwnerRecoveryID, TrackIdentity, the reaper/FileStore plumbing in workers.go, the receipt-driven RecoverRetiredCredentialOwners machinery (credential_recovery.go), and TakeoverRetiredAccountMutationPage's receipt scan (:205).
- Replace with an adoption pass in Start: pool.Manager.AdoptForeignLanes(ctx) (internal/pool/credential_recovery.go rewritten): page three new store queries — CredentialOperationsNotOwnedBy(self, afterAccountID, limit), AccountMutationsNotOwnedBy, PendingAddReservationsNotOwnedBy (foreign = owner_record <> my bytes; the WHERE flips from owner_record=?) — and per row run the domain logic recoverCredentialOperation keeps (pool/credential_operation.go:1465-1504, minus the receipt parameter): account-identity re-check, TakeoverCredentialOperation(fence-from-row, self) where fence.Owner is the row's opaque bytes echoed into the CAS, then abandon prepared no-I/O lanes / resume the rest. Pending adds keep the RetirePendingAdd proof hook. Wire it exactly where the old recovery ran: the new Start, before the scheduler and before business admission opens (ready = Start returned; today transport.go:212-245).

### Two-owner exclusion — the takeover walk, old vs new

Old: (1) A owns rows; (2) A dies; (3) B's reaper probes A's tracked identity, observes absence, mints durable ReapReceipt{Record: A}; (4) B verifies the receipt and CASes each row's epoch A→B; (5) a straggler write under A's fence hits rows-affected=0 → ErrCredentialOperationOwner; (6) the receipt is acked only when zero A-owned rows remain, so a crash mid-recovery re-presents the work.

New, step by step:
1. Only the daemon process writes owner-keyed rows. Today every Begin* owner comes from Manager.credentialOwnerRecord, daemon-gated (manager.go:25, :44); the synckit-helper runtime never mints one (workers.go:119 OpenHostSyncHelperOwners has no TrackIdentity, and its successor is synckit v0.37's Prepare(daemonkit.Ctx) hook); scripts/sync-sim/seed fabricates owners for simulation only. A verification step asserts this stays true.
2. At most one daemon process exists per label: daemonkit.Serve step 2's inode flock, acquired before recovery and Start, ErrBusy on a live incumbent, no takeover verb (daemonkit docs/DESIGN.md §5.1). The flock is released only when drain fully settles; a wedged drain lands stages in Drained.Abandoned, deliberately retains the flock, and launchd's ExitTimeOut SIGKILLs — the successor cannot acquire until the incumbent PROCESS is gone.
3. Therefore when the successor's Start runs, every foreign-owned row's owner is either a dead process or a fully drained one — and cc-pool's Product.Drain (D) stops the scheduler and joins the saga WaitGroup (internal/daemon/server.go's s.wg) before returning, so "fully drained" means no saga goroutine remains.
4. The epoch CAS is unchanged and stays the belt for the impossible straggler: any write under a superseded fence still fails on rows-affected=0.
5. Crash mid-adoption: adoption is a per-row CAS; un-adopted rows stay foreign and the next Start's scan re-presents them. The durable work list is the rows themselves — strictly stronger than the receipt feed, which could name owners whose rows were already settled.
6. Begin-time protection is preserved: BeginCredentialOperation still refuses a foreign-owned lane with ErrCredentialOperationRecoveryRequired (:420, :441, :546 semantics; the comparison is now bytes-vs-self), and executeCredentialOperation's wait/retry arms (pool/credential_operation.go:348-401) keep handling it.

Deliberately NOT rebuilt: a durable acknowledgeable reap-receipt feed. Once rows are the work list nothing consumes receipts; per daemonkit DESIGN.md §6, "the record's absence asserts what a receipt asserted." If a future consumer needs reap durability rows cannot express, cc-pool owns that persistence via daemonkit/durable then — not now.

Also under A (daemon identity and boot, where ownership starts):
- internal/daemon/spec.go (new): one `func Spec(program daemonkit.Program) daemonkit.Daemon` — Label "com.yasyf.cc-pool" (protocol.go:24 ServiceRoleID); Program daemonkit.Stable() (the stable exec path TCC grants key on — memory 1d978f2; today's plist runs the brew Mach-O via ccpAgent, internal/cli/service.go:61-75); Schemas from wirebuildgen (D); Restart: daemonkit.RestartAlways stated explicitly (fusekit b313adf holder/runtime.go:163 precedent — see traps); Shutdown/Handshake/MaxFrame/Concurrency stated from current values (daemonShutdownTimeout, the retired ladder's ceilings); Trust{Serving: daemonkit.ServingSameUser() (a Homebrew tool — the named waiver, stated), Control: &daemonkit.Requirement{TeamID: ServiceTeamID, SigningIdentifier: ServiceRoleID} (successor of the Stop/Receipt/Readiness role table, transport.go:196-209), Business: nil (successor of AllowUnprotected: true)}.
- internal/cli/service.go: install/uninstall/status rebuild on daemonkit.Open(Spec) + Ensure/Control; ccpAgent, daemonServiceControllerConfig (:88), the plist adaptation + Homebrew-formula service-block lockstep (cc-pool doc 3762436) retire — Ensure owns the plist. The SingleEntrant/evict/step-aside machinery in internal/daemon/server.go and peer.go deletes with it.
- The trustroles residuals the mechanical lane froze: internal/statusapp/hooks.go:123,127 stop path → daemonkit Open(Spec) → Control(ctx) → Drain (roles dissolve into the Control lane); internal/holderbridge/deployment_identity.go:249-251,307 → retype the three role fields plus deploymentQuiescePolicy.ControlRole as a cc-pool-local `type PolicyRole string` with the SAME serialized values, so cc-pool's deployment policy JSON bytes — and the startup policy digest they feed — do not change at the flag day.
- internal/store/store.go:28, :444-446 lifecycleLock (proc.FileLockShared): delete. The mechanical lane measured that nothing takes the exclusive side; a shared lock with no exclusive writer guards nothing. SQLite's own locking remains the store's concurrency control. The read-only Lstat probe (:440) goes with it.

## B. Upgrade story for live data — adopt, don't migrate

Decision: compat-free opaque-bytes adoption — the upgrade IS the crash-takeover path. No one-time row rewrite, no compat read path, no quiesce step.

Why, with evidence from the resume code:
- Nothing in the resume path needs to DECODE the old owner; it needs to (a) find foreign rows and (b) echo their owner bytes into the epoch CAS. CredentialOperationsOwnedBy / …NotOwnedBy match on bytes; TakeoverCredentialOperation's WHERE takes the bytes just read from the row (:1113-1119). scanCredentialOperation's decode (:1816 → decodeCredentialOwner :2726) exists only to re-encode for comparisons — with OwnerRecord it reads the column raw and never fails on era.
- Sequence on a real machine: Ensure drains the v0.20.9 daemon; the new build starts; Serve settles prior children; Start mints the v2 owner; AdoptForeignLanes pages every row whose owner_record != the v2 bytes — every old proc.Record row qualifies, byte-for-byte as stored — CASes epoch+1 onto each, then resumes exactly as recoverRetiredCredentialOperation does today (pool/credential_operation.go:1499-1504): prepared non-remove lanes abandon (:1199 path), applying/applied lanes settle against the keychain, account mutations re-enter their state machines, pending_adds retire via RetirePendingAdd. In-flight sagas resume, not orphan.
- The v2 encoding is deliberately un-confusable: it lacks recovery_id, so v0.20.9's Record.Validate rejects it (proc/reaper.go:99-104 requires RecoveryID), and it carries "v":2, which no proc.Record era ever wrote.

Failure modes, named:
- Crash mid-adoption: per-row CAS; remaining old-format rows are still foreign at the next boot; the re-scan re-presents them. No partially-migrated state can exist because there is no migration state — only adopted rows and not-yet-adopted rows, both valid.
- Race with a not-quite-dead old daemon: excluded past Serve's flock (A.2/A.3); belt: a v0.20.9 straggler's fenced writes CAS on (old bytes, old epoch) and lose after adoption bumps the epoch.
- Downgrade after adoption: v0.20.9's decodeCredentialOwner unmarshals v2 bytes into proc.Record and Validate fails → "credential operation owner is corrupt" → those lanes error until cleared. Stated and accepted: fleet policy is fix-forward (daemonkit DESIGN.md §8 gate 1 — v0.21.x, never a re-cut); the operator recovery for a forced downgrade is deleting the in-flight lane rows (each saga is idempotent from its intent/receipt digests, so re-running is safe) — a runbook if it ever happens, not code.
- Stale v0.20.9 stores: the old FileStore files (DisposableWorkerStorePath etc.) stop being read; daemonkit's own legacy sweep (DESIGN.md §8 gate 2) covers its bbolt, and cc-pool's leftover store files are doctor/uninstall cleanup, not load-bearing.

## C. Pool policy

Shape and caps survive; the substrate flips to Ctx:

- internal/workerexec/runner.go: Runner keeps its one method on cc-pool-owned values — Run(ctx, workerexec.CommandRequest) (workerexec.CommandResult, error); CommandRequest{Path, Dir, Args, Env, Stdin []byte, TotalTimeout} and CommandResult{Stdout, Stderr, ExitCode} mirror the v0.20.9 fields minus Receipt (daemonkit@v0.20.9/worker/pool.go:67-82) — the ~30 pass-through sites rename imports only.
- internal/pool/workers.go rewrites: workerRuntime drops pool/children/reaper/owner/claim for a Ctx-backed run surface; newProcessRuntimeAt/newWorkerRuntimeAt collapse. Scheduling is cc-pool's, per the migration guide: a Capacity-4 execution semaphore plus a QueueCapacity-4 admission bound (the chan-struct{} pair worker.Pool itself used, v0.20.9 pool.go:101-102 — about 40 lines), with cc-pool-minted sentinels workerexec.ErrCapacity / ErrTimedOut (the only fleet matcher on the old vocabulary is scripts/vm/helpers/worker-deadline/main.go:104). Caps keep their values (workers.go:16-22): MaxTotalRun 31m via context.WithTimeout inside Run; 16 MiB stdin enforced before dispatch; Cmd.MaxStdout/MaxStderr = 16 MiB.
- Spawn via Ctx.Run, not OwnProcesses. Reasons: the daemon already holds Ctx from Start; Ctx.Run is exactly "one bounded disposable command, reap included" under a deadline-carrying ctx — the 31m cap's natural home; and a second OwnProcesses scope would mean a second record file whose orphans Serve's recovery does NOT settle, whereas Ctx children ride the daemon's record file and crashed generations come back as Ctx.Reclaimed before Start. Long-lived children (accountterminal PTY logins, holder session children) use Ctx.Spawn with Cmd.Session: true so the dedicated session id stays durable kill identity for the whole tree. OwnProcesses(ctx, recordPath) is for non-daemon binaries only (scripts/vm/helpers/worker-deadline, scripts/sync-sim/seed); plain os/exec where nothing needs owning.
- The synckit helper: helperruntime v0.37.1's Config{..., Prepare func(daemonkit.Ctx)} hands the helper its own Ctx — HostSyncHelperOwners (workers.go:119-137) deletes; internal/hostsync builds its Runner over that Ctx.
- The .test re-exec seam survives unchanged: the disposable worker is executable = os.Executable() resolved once at construction (workers.go:109), invoked with procscan's worker sentinel args (cmd/cc-pool/main.go:71-72 IsWorkerInvocation/RunWorker; request on stdin, result on stdout). The Runner fills Cmd{Path: executable, Args: workerArgs, Stdin: encoded request}. Under test the .test binary re-execs and TestMain's env-var branch dispatches — the fork-bomb hazard and the scripts/test.sh harness rule are untouched.
- procscan: the Claude-session scanner (select.go, heartbeat.go, syncworker.go — business logic) survives whole. procscan.WorkerScanner (workers.go:80) retires from the hot path: v0.21 spawns suspended until the record fsyncs, so an untracked worker cannot exist, and Serve settles crashed generations before Start; keep the scan only if cc-pool doctor surfaces it, else delete.

## D. Observation lane — poll-unary

Withdrawn: wire.Server + wire.NewRuntime + ObservationRoute + StreamResponse (internal/daemon/transport.go:53-105, :107-130; account_mutation.go:99). Successor, per fusekit b313adf catalogservice (broker_poll.go, handles.go) and cc-orchestrate ptyhost (opCapture — poll-unary capture instead of pushed updates):

- Server: internal/daemon.Server implements daemonkit.Product. Handle(ctx, req) dispatches on req.Op through the existing Op table (protocol.go:39-61) — s.dispatch survives; the wire.HandlerSpec registration loop (transport.go:66-89) deletes. Drain(Budget) stops intake at the scheduler, cancels execCtx, and joins s.wg (today's settle-before-cancel choreography) — this join is load-bearing for A.3. Close(Budget) closes the store and the holder session. The per-op ladder (operationLadder, transport.go:25-51) deletes: the server inherits each client's conveyed deadline in Handle's ctx; the ladder's client column moves to per-call context.WithTimeout at the CLI Call sites. The CLI/statusapp clients (wire.RuntimeClientConfig/ClientConfig/UnixDialer) rebuild on daemonkit.Open(Spec) + Call.
- Health: the OpHealth ObservationRoute becomes the native verb. Start captures Ctx.Report and publishes the HealthResponse JSON (protocol.go:177) verbatim as Health.Detail on every heartbeat/state change; clients use Client.Health (floor-only, answers during drain). OpHealth, HealthRequest, daemonHealthMaxResponse, daemonHealthObservation delete.
- Account mutation goes poll-unary. handleAccountMutationWire's StreamResponse splits:
  - OpAccountMutation stays unary and non-parking for StartOrAttach / ProvideInput / Cancel (validateAccountMutationCommand unchanged, account_mutation.go:102-136); StartOrAttach returns the fence + current state immediately instead of holding a stream.
  - New OpAccountMutationPoll {Fence, TerminalCursor} → {Chunks, NextCursor, State, Done}: pages accountterminal's replay cursor (the machinery TestTerminalExactReplayCursorAndSettledAcknowledgement proves, internal/accountterminal/terminal_test.go:395; TerminalChunkSize 32 KiB, terminal.go:22). An empty page parks on the terminal's wake channel with a reply margin withheld (pollReplyMargin 500ms — fusekit broker_poll.go:15-16) under the request ctx.
  - Drain-release (the cookiesync finding): every parked poll selects on Ctx.Context.Done() — cancelled at drain-begin — and returns its empty page immediately with State reflecting the drain, so the drain's requests share is never spent waiting out parked polls; the next poll is refused at admission as Draining. The same select releases on Request.Session.Done() (fusekit handles.go bindSession/dropSession precedent), which becomes the attachment-teardown signal replacing stream-connection death — the a2daa70 ptyrelay teardown semantics carry over onto TerminalDisconnectPolicy. OpAccountMutationAck stays unary as-is.
  - Client half: the mutation TUI's TerminalClientEndpoint (internal/accountterminal/client.go:20) pumps Send→ProvideInput and Receive→Poll.
- wirebuildgen revs; the gate stays. The tool (internal/daemon/wirebuildgen/main.go) keeps hashing protocol.go's canonical wire shape but emits `const RuntimeSchema daemonkit.Schema = "com.yasyf.cc-pool.control/<sha256>/v2"` into wirebuild_gen.go (today's WireBuild const, wirebuild_gen.go:5, retires with wire.Server). Daemon.Schemas = []daemonkit.Schema{RuntimeSchema}; era rejection moves to business-attach set membership. The hash input changes with the op-table changes above, so the identity revs by construction; ci.yml:46's `go run ./internal/daemon/wirebuildgen -check` drift gate is unchanged. Skew-tolerant lifecycle probing (doc 3762436) is daemonkit's now: Health/Probe are floor-only native verbs.

## Covered by the mechanical lane — do not re-plan (note 0f6686e, dk-v021-migration @ bf52839)

Trust two-lane collapse (holder.RuntimeTrust, holderbridge.RuntimeTrust, daemonkit.Requirement), the revved fusekit runtime policy digest (cca1c08f…), holder.Config StopControlStore removal, hostsync registry flock → durable.AcquireLock with derived deadlines, pins daemonkit v0.21.3 + synckit v0.37.1 + the fusekit go.work overlay pending v1.16.0, CI cancel-in-progress, the Swift DaemonKit pin 0.21.3, both verify-suite-pins scripts green. Its deliberately-frozen residuals — statusapp/hooks roles, holderbridge deployment_identity roles, the store lifecycleLock, credential_locks — are decided above (A).

## The three migration-guide traps, preserved

1. MaxDetail pin test: size Daemon.MaxFrame from the largest poll page (32 KiB terminal chunks × the page bound, plus StatusSnapshot), and assert daemonkit.MaxDetail(spec.MaxFrame) >= maxPayload in internal/daemon/spec_test.go, so the 4 KiB envelope + base64 reserve can never silently shrink the ceiling.
2. Markerless plists: every pre-upgrade machine's com.yasyf.cc-pool plist lacks DAEMONKIT_AGENT_OWNER; uninstall and upgrade-stop route ONLY through Client.Stop (which falls back to launchd.RemoveUnmarked on ErrNotOwned) — no direct launchd.Remove call site in internal/cli/service.go's uninstall path.
3. Restart stated: Restart: daemonkit.RestartAlways, explicit in Spec (the zero value silently means RestartNever). The old RestartOnFailure existed so a takeover step-aside's clean exit was not relaunched (ccpAgent, cli/service.go:70; doc 3762436 lockstep) — takeover is deleted, upgrades are Ensure-driven (place binary at the stable path → drain → launchd relaunches the new build), and the fleet precedent is holder/runtime.go:163. The formula service block + plist adaptation lockstep retires with it.

## Verification

- scripts/test.sh -race -count=1 ./... (never bare go test — C's .test re-exec seam keeps the harness mandatory).
- Two-owner exclusion: spawn a real daemon child (self-exec), SIGKILL it between Stage and Applied, boot a successor on the same store; assert the lane resumes with exactly one epoch bump, then replay a write under the stale fence and assert ErrCredentialOperationOwner.
- Upgrade fixture: seed credential_operations/account_mutations/pending_adds rows whose owner_record bytes are literal v0.20.9 proc.Record JSON (golden fixture), boot the new daemon, assert every row adopts (epoch+1, v2 owner bytes) and terminals settle — proves B on CI without a real machine.
- wirebuildgen -check green after the op-table change; the MaxDetail pin test; a drain test that parks an OpAccountMutationPoll and asserts it returns within pollReplyMargin of drain-begin, not at its deadline.
